Mostly academia: University of Oxford, University of Edinburgh, TU Munich, National University of Singapore, MBZUAI, Carnegie Mellon University; one independent researcher; industry: MemoraX AI (one author)

Proposes an evaluation method (benchmark SWE-ContextBench and SWE-ContextBench Lite for cross-task context learning); secondary: compares (five coding agents with/without oracle summaries; five context-reuse settings; memory retrieval frameworks)

No SDD approach. Context-reuse settings: No-Context (baseline), Free Context Learning, Oracle Context Learning, Free Summary Learning, Oracle Summary Learning; memory retrieval frameworks: Mem0, OpenViking, LangMem, Supermemory (no versions)

Context pool of prior agent trajectories (tool calls, file navigation, reasoning) from 1,100 experience tasks; summary context pool (final summary paragraph of each trajectory, avg 217.1 tokens vs 25,633.7 for full trajectories); memories extracted/indexed by memory frameworks

Criterion: task resolved (FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS pass). Study 1 (related tasks; task set implied 376), resolved % / cost USD, baseline -> oracle summary: (a) Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 4.5: 19.68 / 0.67 -> 23.40 / 0.55; (b) Codex + GPT-5.3 Codex: 22.60 / 0.31 -> 23.94 / 0.27; (c) Qwen Code + Qwen3.5-plus: 16.22 / 0.33 -> 21.54 / 0.18; (d) Qwen Code + GLM-5: 18.35 / 0.58 -> 19.41 / 0.48; (e) Claude Code + MiniMax 2.7: 19.68 / 0.65 -> 22.07 / 0.46. Oracle summary: quality works (modest), cost works for all. Study 2 (SWE-ContextBench Lite, 99 tasks, Claude Sonnet 4.5; agent not restated), resolved % / time min / cost USD: No-Context 26.26 / 6.37 / 0.79 (baseline); Free Context 26.26 / 6.78 / 0.98 (quality does not work, cost does not work); Oracle Context 27.27 / 5.95 / 0.77 (partly, works); Free Summary 22.22 / 6.28 / 0.91 (does not work, does not work); Oracle Summary 34.34 / 6.66 / 0.85 (works, partly); Mem0 24.24 / 4.72 / 0.62 (does not work, works); OpenViking 29.20 / 4.20 / 0.53 (partly, works); Supermemory 30.30 / 5.04 / 0.58 (works, works); LangMem: retrieval match only (73.34% overall), no resolution reported

Study 1: 5 agent+model configurations x {baseline, oracle summary}. Study 2: Claude Sonnet 4.5 x 5 context settings on 99 Lite tasks (495 runs) + memory frameworks. Baseline: No-Context. Held constant: task prompt template (repo, base commit, problem statement), fresh isolated environment, git history removed, no state carryover. Acceptance tests: FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS from the PR test patch. Repetitions: not stated (apparently one run per task). Human intervention: none

Oracle summaries improved resolution for all five agents (+1.1 to +5.3 points) and lowered cost; best GPT-5.3 Codex 23.94%. On Lite: Oracle Summary best resolution (34.34% vs 26.26%, +8.08); Oracle Context lowest time and cost (5.95 min, 0.77 USD); Free Context +27.3% cost with no gain; Free Summary below baseline; Supermemory best framework (30.30%), OpenViking cheapest (0.53 USD). No significance tests despite 'significantly improve' in the abstract

Distinguished oracle vs free context and frameworks on resolution and cost. Repeatability: single runs, no variance reported; prompt template given. Limitations stated: no comprehensive human validation of problem statements, test patches or solvability; context pool quality not filtered (noisy trajectories)

Context helps only when compact and correctly selected; free retrieval can hurt. Gaps: summarization quality, structured context management, adaptive decisions on when to reuse, adaptive retrieval, critical use of retrieved context; limitation: lack of human validation of tasks
